transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-15
- Time: 9:00 AM PDT / 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~46 minutes (recording started at 9:02)
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Hannah (Redwood CSM), Priya (AquilaWorks Head of ML), Tom (Platform), Lena (SecOps), Oliver (PM)

Summary:
Maya: quick intro, agenda and outcomes we want today — align on pilot scope, timeline, security requirements, and immediate next steps.
Priya: want to validate latency and cost for their customer-facing summarization API and evaluate private deployment inside their VPC.

00:00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick off with a 3 minute overview of what Redwood is doing here and then hand over to Diego for the tech rundown.
00:00:22 Speaker 2 (Priya): Hi, thanks. Quick fyi, we have a hard date, we want to run a pilot by early sept, that's because of our Q3 roadmap.
00:00:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): Got it, early Sept is doable, we'll map out milestones. First, roll call - names and roles?
00:00:50 Speaker 3 (Tom): Tom, platform engineer, I'll be lead on networking and infra.
00:00:57 Speaker 4 (Lena): Lena, SecOps, I'll be owning security/compliance questions.
00:01:02 Speaker 5 (Oliver): Oliver, PM on the product team.
00:01:07 Speaker 6 (Diego): Diego, Solutions Eng for Redwood. I'll handle the nitty gritty on runtime, KV cache, and private deploy constraints.
00:01:15 Speaker 7 (Hannah): Hannah, CSM, I'll run the onboarding flow and ensure milestones are hit.

00:01:30 Speaker 6 (Diego): Quick tech rundown: Redwood has hosted API, dedicated pools, and private (VPC) deployment. For your summarization use case we usually recommend starting on a dedicated pool for throughput then evaluating private if you need data egress control. The important bits: token distribution, max seq length for summaries, and whether you need streaming.
00:02:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): We stream to customers, yes. Typical document size is 2–4k tokens pre-summarization, output ~200–400 tokens. Latency target is p95 sub-800ms for a single request.
00:02:26 Speaker 6 (Diego): okay that's helpful. Our quantized variants can usually hit those numbers on A100/RTX-class infra with continuous batching if you accept slight cost tradeoffs; we'll outline expected per-call token cost in the runbook.

00:03:12 Speaker 4 (Lena): Security first: do you have SOC 2 type 2, we also need audit logs, KMS integrations, and proof that KV cache doesn't leak data between tenants. Also can you support customer-managed keys in the private deployment?
00:03:35 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood is SOC 2 in production, we have KMS integrations and audit trails; for private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM options in the private plane, yep. We'll share the security pack.
00:03:52 Speaker 4 (Lena): and egress — we need to ensure no outbound egress to a shared host in the hosted model, which is why private is preferable.
00:04:03 Speaker 6 (Diego): For private, you run our control plane hooks within your VPC or we run a customer-controlled relay; traffic never leaves your cloud region unless you allow it. We'll sketch the network flow in Diagrams.

00:04:44 Speaker 5 (Oliver): Who are the stakeholders internally? I want to make sure sign-offs are covered.
00:04:50 Speaker 2 (Priya): I'll own the pilot success metrics (quality + latency). Tom will own infra readiness. Lena owns security sign-off. Finance will review cost once you share numbers.

00:05:10 Speaker 6 (Diego): Pilot success criteria — is it quality-based or SLO-based?
00:05:15 Speaker 2 (Priya): Both. We need ROUGE-ish style score maintained against baseline and p95 latency < 800ms for 95% of calls during load tests. Also, cost per 1M tokens should be within the number we'll share.
00:05:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): Cool, we'll propose an eval plan: baseline prompting, 1 week smoke tests on hosted, then 2 week dedicated capacity soak, then private pilot if required.

00:06:05 Speaker 3 (Tom): On the network side: for private we'll need CIDR ranges, egress rules, and an allowed list of IPs for any agent updates. What’s the cadence for patches and runtime updates?
00:06:20 Speaker 6 (Diego): We do rolling updates with canaries. For private deployments we can coordinate maintenance windows; for dedicated hosted pools updates are more frequent but we give notice. We'll provide an ops calendar.

00:06:50 Speaker 4 (Lena): Also need encryption at rest confirmation and key rotation policy. Who rotates keys?
00:06:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): Customer-managed KMS means you control rotation. We'll integrate via Cloud KMS or HSM, and we have a documented key rotation handshake.

00:07:20 Speaker 7 (Hannah): Onboarding timeline suggestion: Week 1: network and access setup; Week 2: pilot data ingestion, sample prompts; Week 3: run smoke tests; Week 4–6: dedicated soak and evaluation; Week 7: review and decide on private -> target pilot start in August to meet early Sept go-live. Does that match?
00:07:47 Speaker 2 (Priya): Yes that aligns but can we accelerate week 1? We can prioritize network and give you a stubbed prompt corpus this week.
00:07:57 Speaker 7 (Hannah): Great, that'll help.

00:08:10 Speaker 6 (Diego): A few technical clarifications I want: do you plan to use prefix caching or full KV caching? That impacts KV memory and warmup times.
00:08:20 Speaker 2 (Priya): We'll likely do prefix caching for sections that repeat across docs — we can iterate.
00:08:28 Speaker 6 (Diego): Noted. Also your expected concurrency?
00:08:33 Speaker 2 (Priya): During spikes up to 350 concurrent requests, sustained ~80–120 normally.
00:08:41 Speaker 6 (Diego): Good call. We'll map capacity to QPS and latency SLOs.

00:09:05 Speaker 3 (Tom): On routing: do you support fallback to smaller models on overload? We want graceful degradation rather than errors.
00:09:14 Speaker 6 (Diego): Yes, smart routing can fallback to cheaper model variants or queued capacity policies; we can configure automatic fallback rules per route.

00:09:40 Speaker 5 (Oliver): Curious about observability — can we get per-token cost breakdowns in your console and tracing for bad responses?
00:09:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood Console has token-level cost, per-route latency breakdown, and trace hooks you can integrate into your tracing stack. We'll give a demo link.

00:10:10 Speaker 4 (Lena): For compliance, we need access logs retained for 1 year. Is retention configurable?
00:10:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, retention is a configurable addon for enterprise customers. We'll put details in the security pack.

00:10:35 Speaker 6 (Diego): Notes from the runtime perspective: for 2–4k token inputs, you may see cold-start latency for KV warmup, but continuous batching and prefix caching helps. Quantization may improve throughput but can slightly impact quality; we'll include quality regression alerting in Optimize.
00:11:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): We'll accept a small quality delta if cost savings are meaningful. Need guidance on threshold.
00:11:12 Speaker 6 (Diego): We'll propose thresholds: if ROUGE drops > 2 points or user-reported degradation > X we'll roll back quantization.

00:11:38 Speaker 7 (Hannah): Operational handoff: I'll be your main CS contact — weekly 30m syncs during the onboarding sprint and then monthly after pilot. Who will be the emergency contact on Redwood side?
00:11:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): Diego is the SE on-call for the pilot; for escalations you can page the support rota. We'll share the rota.

00:12:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): A couple of blockers: we need a legal review of the data flow and an indication of whether you do any model weights retention — do you store customer data for training?
00:12:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): We do not train on customer data by default. Hosted model catalog uses open models; we can sign a clause for no-training on customer data. We'll share the DPA and data handling docs.
00:12:36 Speaker 4 (Lena): Can you produce an attestation that customer prompts won't be used to further train public models?
00:12:43 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, attestation available. We'll include that in the security packet.

00:13:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): For throughput testing, could Redwood run a load test from within our VPC or do you prefer a synthetic test from your side?
00:13:18 Speaker 6 (Diego): We can support both. For private pilot we prefer load generation from within your VPC to validate network paths. We can provide a load harness and run a joint test.

00:13:50 Speaker 3 (Tom): Network specifics: which ports, and do you require hostnames or IP allowlist?
00:13:58 Speaker 6 (Diego): We'll provide an allowlist of egress IPs and a list of ports (usually 443 for HTTPS; some control channels open on x port but we'll send exact list). For private, you won't need egress except for control-plane heartbeat if you allow it.

00:14:30 Speaker 5 (Oliver): Any recommended metrics we should capture on our side during pilot?
00:14:38 Speaker 6 (Diego): Capture request/response latencies, input/output token size, success/error codes, and user-satisfaction proxy if you have it. We'll align on naming conventions for traces.

00:15:12 Speaker 7 (Hannah): Admin access: who needs Console admin, and can we map roles to Okta groups?
00:15:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): We support SSO SAML/Okta and RBAC; you can map groups to roles. We'll include a recommended role matrix.

00:15:45 Speaker 4 (Lena): If we do private deploy, are there any known regulatory issues with running in our region EU-west?
00:15:55 Speaker 6 (Diego): We support EU region deployments and can keep data residency inside your region; we'll confirm encryption in transit/rest compliance and local legal nuances in the security doc.

00:16:20 Speaker 2 (Priya): Let's talk about success metrics concretely: propose we run an A/B on quality during dedicated soak with control being our current in-house summarizer.
00:16:31 Speaker 6 (Diego): Good plan. We'll help set up eval harness and automated regression alerts.

00:17:00 Speaker 5 (Oliver): Pricing question quick — what's the delta between dedicated pool and private deployment?
00:17:08 Speaker 1 (Maya): Dedicated is usage plus capacity commitment; private has a platform fee and additional infra & support costs. We'll send a detailed pricing sheet.

00:17:30 Speaker 2 (Priya): Competitor note — we looked at ManagedOpenAI; they were cheaper but lacked private options and had less observability.
00:17:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. We'll highlight differences in the one-pager.

00:18:05 Speaker 6 (Diego): Technical deep dive plan: after we ingest your prompt corpus and sample payloads, I'll run a small benchmark to give expected p95 latency and token cost for each model variant.
00:18:20 Speaker 2 (Priya): We'll aim to provide that corpus by Friday.

00:18:40 Speaker 7 (Hannah): Let's lock next meeting: propose a network intake meeting Tuesday 2026-06-17 10:00am PT for Diego and Tom to walk the CIDR and firewall rules.
00:18:54 Speaker 3 (Tom): That works.
00:19:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): I'll send calendar invites and the onboarding runbook.

00:19:18 Speaker 4 (Lena): One more — do you maintain a list of sub-processing vendors? We need disclosures for any third-party infra.
00:19:27 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we'll attach a vendor list and their compliance attestations.

00:19:40 Speaker 6 (Diego): Small implementation note: depending on chosen quantization we may propose 4-bit for inference to reduce memory footprint; we'll show quality-impact graphs.
00:19:55 Speaker 2 (Priya): Fine as long as we have rollback triggers.

00:20:10 Speaker 5 (Oliver): Any recommended guardrails or prompt templates to avoid hallucinations for summarization?
00:20:18 Speaker 6 (Diego): We'll share structured prompt templates and function-calling patterns to force extraction-based summaries. Also suggest policy-based filters for hallucination checks.

00:20:48 Speaker 7 (Hannah): I'm going to summarize next steps now.
00:20:52 Speaker 7 (Hannah): Redwood: share onboarding runbook, security pack, pricing, and allowlist details by 2026-06-18.
00:21:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): AquilaWorks: provide prompt corpus and token volume estimates by 2026-06-22.
00:21:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll also set up a shared drive for artifacts and share access.

00:21:25 Speaker 3 (Tom): small question — do you support private model variants in the private deploy?
00:21:33 Speaker 6 (Diego): Yes, you can bring private variants; we support pinned model versions and can host on-prem variants in the private plane.

00:21:58 Speaker 4 (Lena): compliance Q: will you allow security reviews inside their staging environment?
00:22:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we often do joint security reviews during onboarding. We'll schedule that.

00:22:20 Speaker 5 (Oliver): Are there any prerequisites from our side to expedite?
00:22:26 Speaker 7 (Hannah): Quick list: network contact, sample corpus, access to an Okta admin for SSO setup, and a finance contact.
00:22:38 Speaker 2 (Priya): finance contact is Nora, cc'ing later.

00:22:55 Speaker 6 (Diego): I'll follow up with a preliminary capacity plan tailored to 350 concurrent and the token profiles.

00:23:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): Anything else?
00:23:14 Speaker 5 (Oliver): Not from product.
00:23:17 Speaker 4 (Lena): No, that's all.
00:23:20 Speaker 2 (Priya): One last ask — can we see a small demo of the Console traces?
00:23:26 Speaker 1 (Maya): We can do that in the follow-up — I'll include console screenshots and a short recording.

00:23:40 Speaker 7 (Hannah): Thanks everyone, we’ll send the invites and follow up.
00:23:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks, talk soon.

Notes / Artifacts mentioned:
- Onboarding runbook (link: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/aquilaworks-onboarding)
- Security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/aquilaworks-pack)
summary: Kickoff to align pilot scope (summarization), timeline to reach early Sept, network & security prerequisites for private deployment, and next steps: runbook, security pack, prompt corpus, and a network intake meeting scheduled.
notes: Customer prefers private deployment for egress control but is open to dedicated pool for early evaluation
Team to run joint load test from customer's VPC
Redwood to include flag-based rollback plan for quantization
